title: Read the shape
summary: Shape tells you the size of each dimension. A table-like array has a row count and a column count.
introduction: Shape tells you the size of each dimension. A table-like array has a row count and a column count. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Shape tells you the size of each dimension. A table-like array has a row count and a column count.

blocks.code:
import numpy as np

grid = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
print(grid.shape)
blocks.title: Read the shape

blocks.text: The output is (2, 3): two rows, each with three columns.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw this array as a table on paper.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: The first shape number is not always the total number of values.
For more detail later, use this [NumPy further reading](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/user/absolute_beginners.html).
